newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-Japan eyeglass chain set to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Japan eyeglass chain set to cut costs.

text.p: Japanese eyeglass chain operator Paris Miki Inc says it plans to scale down costs stemming from distribution and building new outlets in order to boost profitability.

"We have ambitions to raise the rate of return on operating profits from the current 12.5 percent to 17.5 percent in five years' time," company president Hiroshi Tane told Reuters in a recent interview.
"In order to compete with large chain stores and foreign firms, we must keep working to strengthen our business," he said.
Tane said that the pillar of the eyeglass vendor's cost-cutting plans would be a widespread use of a computer system to keep track of eyeglass frame and lens inventories.
The system which has already been installed at 415 of its shops, can also be used to help create spectacles according to customers' tastes by using computer graphics.
He added that a new distribution centre in western Japan was coming on stream on Thursday, which would help reduce distribution costs.
Miki is Japan's largest eyeglass retailer in terms of stores and sales. In the year to end-February 1997, parent current profit jumped to 9.07 billion yen from 6.58 billion in the previous year.
Tane said that in the first three months of the new business year, sales were dampened by the two percentage point rise in the national sales tax on April 1.
But by lowering prices, Miki managed to keep business relatively brisk and posted growth of about three percent in sales, he added.
Tane forecasts stiff competition ahead, but said he believes that the industry is far from being saturated.
"The market for eyeglasses is due to grow as the aging population increases in Japan and when looking at the business from a global viewpoint, the potential is immeasurable," Tane said.
"In Japan I envision one shop for every 100,000 people which means that we can build to (a total) 1,333 outlets," he said.

In the year to end-February 1998, Miki, which now has about 700 stores, plans to increase its outlets by 63 while scrapping 15 to 20 stores. Most of the new shops will be built in shopping centres, Tane said.
"We also hope to eventually expand into northern Japan where we have relatively few outlets," Tane said.
"There is a possibility that in the future we may venture into the eyeglass market in Southeast Asia and India," he said.
